state.background: Plan45 proposes B3d as exactly two assertion-level Browser Mode candidates: portrait CAGR sheet row p45-a-cagr-sheet-08 (P42-060–063) and landscape row p45-a-cagr-sheet-09 (P42-064–066). Explorer/source review confirmed the exact Playwright mapping in tests/e2e/cagr-sheet.e2e.spec.ts and the existing Browser Mode fixture mounts actual CagrPanel/useCagrState with deterministic two-row CPI data. The fixture currently uses the default 1280x800 viewport and does not load globals.css, so the plan requires explicit viewport assertions and a bounded, documented CSS fixture baseline. Oracle recommends transferring only sheet-local dialog/result visibility and bottom-bound geometry; production route trigger, live #section-stacked intersection, and page-shell placement remain Playwright-owned. Each stable row remains partial and M stays 1. These are 2 of the next 20 further named Browser Mode cases before one consolidated E2E run.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly two new named Browser Mode tests are proposed, both in tests/browser-mode/CagrPanel.browser.test.tsx, each using the real CagrPanel and useCagrState with deterministic existing chart data.

Portrait row p45-a-cagr-sheet-08 maps P42-060 dialog visible, P42-061 result value visible, P42-062 .cagrResultDetail bottom <= 667, and P42-063 .cagrSheetNote bottom <= 667 from T-E2E-8 at tests/e2e/cagr-sheet.e2e.spec.ts:175. The Browser Mode viewport must be set to and verified as 375x667.

Landscape row p45-a-cagr-sheet-09 maps P42-064 dialog visible, P42-065 result value visible, and P42-066 .cagrResultDetail bottom <= window.innerHeight + 1 (376px) from T-E2E-9 at tests/e2e/cagr-sheet.e2e.spec.ts:205. The Browser Mode viewport must be set to and verified as 667x375.

The Browser Mode fixture does not load globals.css. State an explicit local CSS baseline for relevant document defaults (16px root font size, border-box sizing, zero body margin/padding, and a documented system-font fallback) and limit geometry claims to that fixture baseline; do not claim production page-shell placement.

Keep production page navigation, live #section-stacked intersection/scroll, actual route trigger/location and trigger-to-sheet integration, and page-shell placement in Playwright. If dialog visibility is retained as a route integration smoke after the click, explicitly distinguish that integration owner from the component-local dialog visibility contract.

Only the mapped local dialog/result visibility and bottom-bound assertions may be considered for removal after both focused Browser Mode tests pass and independent review plus an implementation JEV checkpoint pass. All unrelated E2E assertions remain.

These are partial slices: both stable rows remain partial, A=123/E=90/M=1 remains unchanged, and M is not incremented. They count as 2 toward 20 further named Browser Mode migrations before the next consolidated E2E run; run no E2E before those 20 cases pass.

The proposal records BottomSheet geometry context: inline/fixed, max-height 60dvh; compact 45dvh; landscape at <=500px height 70dvh. Component fixtures do not claim production route-fed data, chart intersection, trigger positioning, or page-shell layout.
verification: Source mapping was inspected directly: T-E2E-8 line 175 maps P42-060/-061/-062/-063 to dialog, result value, detail bottom, and note bottom; T-E2E-9 line 205 maps P42-064/-065/-066 to dialog, result value, and detail bottom.

The existing Browser Mode fixture at tests/browser-mode/CagrPanel.browser.test.tsx mounts the actual CagrPanel and useCagrState with deterministic two-row CPI data; its current viewport is the provider default 1280x800. Browser Mode render helper uses Testing Library and setup does not load production globals.css.

Source CSS inspection found global universal border-box and zero margin/padding defaults, and BottomSheet viewport-dependent max heights. These production-shell defaults are not silently assumed by the current Browser Mode fixture.
knownConstraints: Browser Mode validates the component-local fixture, not live intersection of #section-stacked, real route data, production trigger position, or page-shell placement.
Typography or computed geometry can differ if the fixture CSS baseline diverges from production; bound the claim to the declared fixture baseline and retain integration/layout guarantees in E2E.
No implementation or test evidence exists for B3d yet. The proposed E2E deletion is conditional on focused tests, independent review, and the later implementation checkpoint.
state.outputRequirement: Assess this exact two-row viewport-pair proposal under the stated scope. Select exactly one criterion from the supplied set. If not valid_as_defined, identify one case-specific finding and affected row/assertion, observed evidence or exact neededEvidence, concrete proposedFix/nextAction, and remainingUncertainty. Do not treat either row as fully migrated or authorize E2E before the 20-case gate.

plan.instructions: Select exactly one mutually exclusive criterion for this B3d plan checkpoint.

criteria.valid_as_defined: The bounded two-row viewport-pair plan is sufficiently specified and respects the stated ownership boundaries.
criteria.requirements_mismatch: The proposed transfer or retained ownership contradicts an applicable requirement.
criteria.missing_prerequisites_info: Prerequisite facts needed to assess the plan are missing.
criteria.incomplete_implementation_info: The plan lacks implementation detail needed to assess feasibility or scope.
criteria.implementation_issue: A concrete implementation or source constraint invalidates the proposed plan.
criteria.scope_violation: The plan exceeds the two-row assertion slices or weakens required E2E boundaries.
criteria.other: A material plan issue does not fit the other criteria.
criteria.indeterminate: The available evidence does not support a reliable determination.
